name: The legal buffer distance, and which one to test

identity.method_name: Statutory/judicial buffer (no-construction setback) distance for Bengaluru lakes and rajakaluves
identity.core_idea: This is not a model but the legal parameter that defines the 'fence' polygon the whole geo-fencing deliverable is built around: how many metres outward from a lake's boundary counts as protected land, such that any building footprint or water-loss inside that ring is presented as encroachment-relevant. There is no single number. Four different regimes have applied to Bengaluru lakes at different times, from different authorities, for different purposes, and the most recent one is a size-tiered table (not a flat distance) that took legal effect on 18 February 2026 -- seven months before this research was done.
identity.official_dataset_ids: Not a dataset; the operative legal instruments are: (1) Karnataka Tank Conservation and Development Authority Act, 2014, Karnataka Act No. 32 of 2014, s.12(3) (original uniform 30 m rule); (2) National Green Tribunal, Southern Zone, Order dated 4.5.2016 in O.A. No. 222 of 2014, Forward Foundation & Ors. v. State of Karnataka & Ors. (75 m lakes / 50-35-25 m rajakaluves) [verify -- bench and exact OA style confirmed only via secondary citation inside the Supreme Court judgment below, not from the NGT order text itself]; (3) Supreme Court of India, Civil Appeal No. 5016 of 2016 with connected appeals, Mantri Techzone Pvt. Ltd. v. Forward Foundation and Ors., decided 5.3.2019, reported (2019) AIRONLINE 495 SC [verify exact SCC citation]; (4) Bengaluru Revised Master Plan 2015 / draft RMP 2031 zoning regulations (30 m lake buffer measured from the master-plan lake boundary); (5) Karnataka Tank Conservation and Development Authority (Amendment) Act, 2025, Karnataka Act No. 19 of 2026, notified in the Karnataka Gazette Extraordinary of 18.02.2026 (Governor's assent 16.02.2026), substituting s.12(3) with a size-tiered buffer table.

fit_to_project.ground_truth_proxy_strategy: Not applicable in the ML sense -- this item supplies a rule-based spatial parameter (the fence radius), not a label. It functions as a threshold-rule definition of the region-of-interest: everything within the chosen buffer ring is scored as 'protected-zone intrusion,' everything outside is not. Because the legal number itself is contested and has just changed (Feb 2026), the choice of buffer is itself a design decision that must be justified and disclosed, not a free label source.
fit_to_project.input_required: A single per-lake boundary polygon in a projected CRS (the project already has this as the OSM multipolygon, see B2) plus a chosen buffer distance in metres. The project has the polygon; it does not yet have a legally defensible per-lake buffer distance, because the applicable distance now depends on each lake's recorded acreage under the Feb-2026 tiered KTCDA table, which the project has not looked up per lake.
fit_to_project.viable_with_42_rows: yes -- the buffer is a per-lake, not per-lake-year, geometric construct (a shapely/geopandas .buffer() call), so it is defined once per lake (n=6) and reused across all 7 years; it does not consume or depend on the 42-row tabular structure at all.
fit_to_project.viable_without_ground_truth: yes -- constructing the buffer ring requires no encroachment labels, only a boundary polygon and a legal citation for the distance.
fit_to_project.resolution_match_20m: Partially, and this is the most important practical finding of this item. The project's grid is 20 m EPSG:32643. The historic reference figures (30 m Master Plan / SC-reinstated figure, 75 m NGT figure) are both coarse enough to resolve as 1-4 pixel-wide rings. But the buffer distances newly introduced by the Feb-2026 KTCDA amendment for anything under 25 acres (0 m, 1 m, 3 m, 6 m, 12 m) are all sub-pixel or near-sub-pixel at 20 m resolution and cannot be meaningfully rasterised or tested against this imagery. Only lakes whose KTCDA-recorded extent falls in the '25-100 acre' (24 m) or '>100 acre' (30 m) tiers produce a buffer width the project's pixel grid can actually represent.
fit_to_project.label_source_needed: none -- this is a legal/geometric parameter, not a supervised label.
fit_to_project.fixes_which_stated_limitation: none directly, but it gates limitation (3): a geo-fence built on the wrong or unstated buffer distance cannot support any claim of 'illegal encroachment' regardless of how good the underlying water/vegetation classification is, because the panel's first question will be 'illegal under which rule.'
fit_to_project.handles_desilting_confound: no -- the buffer distance says nothing about why water area changed inside the fence; it only defines where the fence sits. Desilting drainage (e.g. Bellandur 15.7 ha to 0.4 ha to 107.9 ha, 2019-2025) will occur inside any of the candidate buffers equally and must be handled by a separate signal (temporal water/vegetation classification), not by the buffer choice.
fit_to_project.handles_hyacinth_confound: no -- same reasoning; the buffer is orthogonal to the water-vs-vegetation classification problem that hyacinth mats create.
fit_to_project.legal_traceability: This field is what the whole item exists to answer. As of September 2026 there is no single 'the' legally binding Bengaluru buffer. Four regimes coexist: (a) Bengaluru Master Plan / RMP 2015, RMP 2031 (draft): a 30 m buffer for lakes measured, per the plan's own drafting language quoted in the Supreme Court judgment, from a fixed reference around the lake (described in secondary sources as 'from the centre'/'from the boundary' inconsistently -- the exact RMP clause text and its stated measurement point could not be independently confirmed from the draft RMP 2031 Volume-6 Zoning Regulations PDF, which was not machine-readable; mark [verify]). (b) NGT order dated 4.5.2016 in O.A. 222 of 2014 (Forward Foundation v. State of Karnataka): 75 m for lakes, 50/35/25 m for primary/secondary/tertiary rajakaluves, measured 'from the periphery'/'from the edge' of the water body/drain -- intended to apply to all Bengaluru lakes and rajakaluves. (c) Supreme Court, Mantri Techzone Pvt. Ltd. v. Forward Foundation (5.3.2019): expressly SET ASIDE the NGT's general 75 m direction for all other Bengaluru developers/lakes ('all the other appeals are hereby allowed and the direction/condition No.(1) in the order dated 4.5.2016 is hereby set aside except the direction issued against respondent Nos. 9 and 10'), while SUSTAINING the 75 m figure specifically and only against the two encroaching parties (Mantri Techzone / Forward Foundation-affected Bellandur-Agara SEZ site), applied retrospectively (demolition ordered) for that site alone. For every other Bengaluru lake, the practical effect is that the pre-2016 Master Plan buffer (commonly cited as 30 m) is what survives, not a court-mandated new figure -- the SC did not itself re-legislate a 30 m rule city-wide, it simply removed the NGT's 75 m general rule and left the RMP figure standing by default. This is frequently mis-reported in secondary sources as the Court having 'reinstated the 30 m Master Plan buffer, prospectively' for all lakes; the primary judgment text extracted here supports 'set aside the general 75 m direction,' which is a related but narrower holding, and the 'prospective, city-wide 30 m' framing should be treated as [verify]. (d) Karnataka Tank Conservation and Development Authority Act, 2014 (Act 32/2014) s.12(3): originally set a flat 30 m 'from the outer boundary of the tanks,' applicable (after the 2018 amendment, Act 15/2018, removed the carve-out for BBMP/BDA areas) within Bengaluru too. (e) THE CURRENTLY BINDING TEXT as of this research date: the Karnataka Tank Conservation and Development Authority (Amendment) Act, 2025 (Karnataka Act No. 19 of 2026), gazetted 18.02.2026, replaced the flat 30 m in s.12(3) with a tiered table measured 'from revenue boundary of the tank': 0 m for tanks up to 0.05 acre, 1 m (0.05-0.10 acre), 3 m (0.10-1.00 acre), 6 m (1-10 acres), 12 m (10-25 acres), 24 m (25-100 acres), 30 m (above 100 acres). This is a statute, applies by its own force to every KTCDA-jurisdiction tank/lake including Bengaluru's, and is the most recent, most specific, and most authoritative currently-in-force text found. It is however only seven months old, was returned once by the Governor for clarification before assent, and the Federation of Bengaluru Lakes has stated it is 'considering challenging the notification,' citing a pending NGT matter -- so its long-term survival is not guaranteed. Measurement basis: the 2025/2026 KTCDA table is explicit -- 'Buffer from revenue boundary of the tank' -- i.e. the Revenue Department's recorded survey/kharab boundary (RTC/Akarband records), NOT the full tank level (FTL) hydrological line and NOT the current water's edge. This is the only one of the four regimes whose measurement reference point is stated unambiguously in the primary text.
fit_to_project.temporal_granularity: The buffer distance itself is not a time-varying quantity within the study window (2019-2025) -- whichever figure is chosen is applied as a single static ring per lake for the whole 7-year series. The one temporal wrinkle is that the applicable LAW changed mid-way through 2026 (after the study's 2019-2025 imagery window ended), so a 2026 write-up must decide whether to apply the rule in force during the years studied (30 m Master Plan / no clean single figure) or the rule in force at the time of reporting (Feb-2026 tiered KTCDA table) -- this should be stated explicitly, not silently assumed.

implementation.libraries: geopandas, shapely (Polygon.buffer()), pyproj/EPSG:32643 for the metric CRS already used by the project. No specialised legal-tech tooling is needed once the distance and boundary source are fixed.
implementation.licence: The underlying legal texts are public government/judicial records: Karnataka Acts and gazette notifications are Government of Karnataka publications with no restriction on citation or reproduction of the legal text itself; Supreme Court and NGT judgments are public record and their text is exempted from copyright restriction for citation under s.52(1)(q) of the Copyright Act, 1957. No licence blocks academic use or quotation of any of the sources cited here.
implementation.compute_requirement: Trivial -- a single .buffer(d) call per lake polygon (n=6), sub-second on a laptop CPU; no GPU, no Colab/Kaggle quota consumed.
implementation.student_days: 0.5-1 day to finalise which distance(s) to test and implement the buffer once a boundary source is fixed (see B2); an additional 1-2 days if the student also looks up each of the 6 lakes' KTCDA-tier-relevant recorded acreage from RTC/Bhoomi records to check which tier applies under the Feb-2026 law, which this research recommends but did not do lake-by-lake.

evaluation.metrics: Not a predictive method, so no accuracy metric applies to the buffer choice itself. The correct evaluation is a sensitivity/robustness analysis: report the 'intrusion area' or 'building count inside fence' result under at least two candidate buffer distances (e.g. 30 m and 75 m) and show how much the headline number changes. A large swing between the two is itself a reportable finding about how buffer-choice-sensitive the whole geo-fencing deliverable is.
evaluation.validation_protocol: Not a train/test-style validation. The applicable protocol is a disclosed multi-buffer sensitivity sweep across all 6 lakes and all 7 years, pre-registered (decided and written down before results are inspected) to avoid choosing whichever buffer makes the encroachment story look best.
evaluation.leakage_risk: The main risk is not statistical leakage but researcher-degrees-of-freedom / confirmation bias: since there is no single correct number, a student could quietly try several buffer widths and report only the one giving the most dramatic (or most defensible-looking) result. This must be pre-disclosed and the sensitivity band reported, not hidden.
evaluation.uncertainty_reporting: Buffer-choice uncertainty should be reported as a band (minimum and maximum 'intrusion' estimate across the 30 m and 75 m reference cases, and separately under the Feb-2026 tiered figure for whichever tier each lake's recorded acreage falls into), not as a single point estimate with no caveat.
evaluation.augmentation_honesty_risk: not applicable -- no synthetic data or augmentation is involved in constructing a buffer polygon.

evidence.published_performance: Not a performance metric. Documented figures found, with sourcing confidence noted: 30 m Master Plan lake buffer (RMP 2015; corroborated independently by the Karnataka High Court's own 2011 committee report, 'Preservation of Lakes in the City of Bangalore' (Justice N.K. Patil Committee, report dated 26.02.2011 pursuant to Karnataka High Court order dated 26.11.2010 in WP No. 817/2008 and others), which states verbatim: 'The present norm of 30 mt buffer surrounding leagal [sic] boundary lakes is a must to preserve the lakes' -- confirmed, high confidence); 75 m NGT buffer for lakes and 50/35/25 m for primary/secondary/tertiary rajakaluves, NGT order dated 4.5.2016 (confirmed via the Supreme Court's own quotation of the NGT order in its 2019 judgment -- confirmed, high confidence, though the NGT order's own full text was not independently retrieved -- [verify] on exact bench/OA citation format); Supreme Court's 2019 disposition setting aside the general 75 m direction while sustaining it against the two named respondents only (confirmed via IndianKanoon-hosted text of Mantri Techzone Pvt. Ltd. v. Forward Foundation, decided 5.3.2019 -- confirmed, moderate-high confidence, obtained via an AI-summarised fetch of the case text rather than a directly read verbatim PDF, so exact paragraph numbering should be treated as [verify]); tiered 0/1/3/6/12/24/30 m buffer by tank size, Karnataka Act No. 19 of 2026 (KTCDA Amendment Act 2025), gazetted 18.02.2026 (confirmed directly from the PRS Legislative Research-hosted bill/act PDF and the gazette notification text reproduced within it -- highest confidence source obtained in this research, essentially primary text).
evidence.study_area_of_that_work: Every source is Bengaluru/Karnataka-specific by construction -- there is no generic national figure being misapplied here; all four regimes were written for, or explicitly extended to, Bengaluru's lakes and rajakaluves.
evidence.applies_to_indian_urban_lakes: yes, directly -- this entire item is Bengaluru-specific statutory and case law, not a transferred or generalised finding from elsewhere.
evidence.evidence_recency: Most recent binding change: 18 February 2026 (KTCDA Amendment Act, Act No. 19 of 2026) -- current at the time of this research (September 2026). Next most recent: Supreme Court judgment, 5 March 2019. Underlying original statute: 2014 (Act 32 of 2014). NGT order: 4 May 2016. None of the load-bearing sources for the 'currently binding' answer are pre-2020; only the corroborating 2011 High Court committee report (used to confirm the pre-2016 30 m baseline) is older, and it is used only as corroboration, not as the operative rule.
evidence.primary_sources: Karnataka Tank Conservation and Development Authority Act, 2014, and (Amendment) Act, 2025 (Act No. 19 of 2026), full bill and gazette text via PRS Legislative Research: https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/acts_states/karnataka/2014/2014KR32.pdf and https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/bills_states/karnataka/2025/Bill33of2025KA.pdf ; news confirmation of gazette date and Act number: https://propheadlines.com/2026/02/20/karnataka-government-notifies-new-lake-buffer-rules-2026/ ; Supreme Court judgment Mantri Techzone Pvt. Ltd. v. Forward Foundation and Ors., 5.3.2019, via IndianKanoon: https://indiankanoon.org/doc/82379995/ ; BBMP's own hosted copy of the NGT/SC judgment: https://site.bbmp.gov.in/documents/NGT%20SC%20Judgement.pdf (fetch failed during this research, not independently re-verified -- [verify]); background on the underlying encroachment (Mantri Techzone/Bellandur-Agara SEZ) via The News Minute: https://www.thenewsminute.com/article/bellandur-agara-encroachment-case-ngt-slaps-rs-5-lakh-fine-mantri-techzone-78010 ; Karnataka High Court Committee Report, 'Preservation of Lakes in the City of Bangalore,' 26.02.2011: https://data.opencity.in/dataset/46dffdd5-1b51-4a72-bdc0-41a0ec85c31c/resource/225ab3a3-e767-4b63-a406-7048712d6b46/download/0634635f-5928-4030-aaea-d125e488aec2.pdf ; SANDRP commentary on the 2025/2026 amendment's environmental criticism and legal-challenge posture: https://sandrp.in/2026/02/10/bengaluru-lakes-2025-buffer-zone-amended-pollution-rising/ ; Mongabay India commentary: https://india.mongabay.com/2025/12/environmentalists-concerned-over-size-based-buffer-zones-for-water-bodies/ .

risk.failure_modes: (1) Assuming a single flat number (e.g. 'the legal buffer is 30 m' or 'the legal buffer is 75 m') without disclosing that the law changed in February 2026 and is now size-tiered -- this is the single most likely error a rushed student makes. (2) Applying the 75 m figure to all six lakes as though the Supreme Court generally reinstated it, when in fact it was sustained only against the two named Mantri Techzone/Forward Foundation parties at one specific site (Bellandur-Agara) and set aside as a general rule everywhere else. (3) Not checking each of the project's 6 lakes' KTCDA-recorded acreage against the new tiered table -- a lake under 25 acres would legally warrant only a 6-12 m buffer, which is below or barely above this project's 20 m pixel size and cannot be meaningfully tested with this imagery; presenting a 30 m or 75 m ring for such a lake would misrepresent the current law. (4) Treating the RMP 2031's own buffer clause as settled without having read its final notified text (the draft Volume-6 Zoning Regulations PDF could not be machine-read in this research).
risk.panel_defensibility: A capstone panel will ask 'which law says that number, and is it still in force?' This item's honest answer -- there are at least four historically-applicable figures, the most current one is a size-tiered table barely seven months old and possibly headed for legal challenge, and the pre-existing 30 m figure is the safest general-purpose fallback for large lakes -- survives that question only if it is stated exactly this way, with the multiplicity disclosed up front, rather than picking one number and hoping it is not probed.
risk.honest_expectation: The project cannot responsibly claim a single 'the legally correct buffer' for all six lakes without lake-by-lake acreage lookup against the Feb-2026 tiered table, which is additional legwork beyond this item's scope. The realistic and defensible outcome is: test 30 m as the primary reference distance (it is the longest-standing figure, corresponds to the RMP/Supreme-Court-surviving default for general application, and also happens to be the top tier -- '>100 acre' -- of the new KTCDA table, which very likely covers Bengaluru's larger lakes such as Bellandur and Varthur), report 75 m as an explicit upper-bound sensitivity case (historically significant, and still literally in force for the one Bellandur-Agara site), and explicitly flag that the Feb-2026 tiered law may require a smaller, sub-pixel buffer for any of the project's lakes recorded under 100 acres -- a null/non-testable result for those lakes at 20 m resolution, which is itself a valid and reportable finding rather than a gap to paper over.

verdict.recommended_rank: adopt-if-time, with mandatory caveats -- test both 30 m and 75 m as bracketing reference distances for all six lakes, and separately look up each lake's KTCDA-tier-relevant acreage to state (not necessarily test, given 20 m pixels) what the Feb-2026 law would actually require for that specific lake.
verdict.one_line_for_the_guide: There is no single legally binding Bengaluru lake buffer distance; the safest defensible choice for this project is to test 30 m (the long-standing Master Plan/KTCDA figure, also the top tier of the brand-new Feb-2026 size-tiered KTCDA law for lakes over 100 acres) and 75 m (the historic NGT figure, still literally binding only at one specific Bellandur-Agara site) as bracketing sensitivity cases, while explicitly disclosing that the size-tiered 2026 amendment may legally require a sub-pixel buffer for smaller lakes in the dataset that this project's 20 m imagery cannot resolve.
